  but the error text told me things docs/ did not.

answers.docs.gaps:
1. Wrong. docs/crates/input/topics/framework-integration.md says: "`standout`
   re-exports `standout-input` as `standout::input`, so a single dependency on
   `standout` is enough". With only `standout` in Cargo.toml, the
   `standout::Questionnaire` and `standout::QuestionnaireChoices` derives fail
   to compile because their expansion names the `standout_input` crate
   directly. A direct `standout-input` dependency is required.

2. Missing. docs/guides/derived-questionnaires.md shows the wired handler as a
   plain `fn import(_matches: &clap::ArgMatches, ctx: &CommandContext)`, but
   never says that the `#[handler]` macro — the shape every other guide leads
   with — cannot be used for a questionnaire command. The failure surfaces as a
   confusing arity error inside the `Dispatch` derive.

3. Missing. Nothing documents that hook order inside `CommandConfig` decides
   whether a `pre_dispatch` hook runs before or after questionnaire resolution.
   It does: a hook registered before `.questionnaire::<T>()` runs before
   collection, and one registered after it runs after, with the typed answers
   already readable via `ctx.questionnaire()`. I established this by
   experiment; the whole design of the two guards depends on it.

4. Missing. `AppBuilder::hooks(path, hooks)` is presented in
   docs/topics/app-configuration.md and execution-model.md as the way to attach
   hooks to a command path, with no warning that for a questionnaire command it
   displaces the framework's own pre-dispatch resolution and breaks the command.

5. Missing. docs/guides/derived-questionnaires.md documents the gate only as
   "Standout asks for an exact `yes` on an attended controlling terminal" and
   offers no way to reword it, relax it, or turn it off, even though
   `questionnaire_with_form_and_review` shows the surrounding steps are
   customizable. There is likewise no public constant or accessor for the
   reserved `--answers` / `--yes` arguments the integration injects, so a hook
   that needs to know whether a sheet was supplied has to inspect
   `ArgMatches::ids()` for a framework-internal id.

6. Stale. The docs pin older versions than the workspace does:
   framework-integration.md says `standout = "7"`, intro-to-input.md says
   `standout-input = "0.1"`, and minimal-single-crate.md says `standout = "7"`,
   while the app builds against 8.1.1. docs/crates/input/topics/input-sources.md
   is stale in a stronger sense — its whole `InputSource::chain()` /
   `InputSource::arg("name")` API disagrees with the `InputChain` /
   `ArgSource::new` API in intro-to-input.md. I did not need either, but a
   reader following input-sources.md would be writing code that does not exist.
answers.friction:
1. The questionnaire derives do not work with only a `standout` dependency.
   `cargo build` failed with:
   "error[E0433]: cannot find `standout_input` in the crate root ... this error
   originates in the derive macro `standout::Questionnaire`". I added
   `standout-input = "=8.1.1"` to Cargo.toml to fix it.

2. `#[handler]` and a questionnaire command do not compose. With
   `#[dispatch(questionnaire = ProvisionAnswers, template = "provision.jinja")]`
   over a `#[handler]`-annotated function, the build failed with:
   "error[E0593]: function is expected to take 2 arguments, but it takes 1
   argument ... required by a bound in `GroupBuilder::command_with`". The fix
   was the plain `fn(&ArgMatches, &CommandContext) -> HandlerResult<T>` shape
   that derived-questionnaires.md shows.

3. `AppBuilder::hooks(...)` silently replaced the questionnaire's own
   pre-dispatch resolution. After adding
   `.hooks("provision", Hooks::new().pre_dispatch(require_answer_source))`,
   a previously working sheet run failed at runtime with:
   "Error: no input named `questionnaire` was registered for this command".
   Registering the hook inside `command_with`'s `CommandConfig` instead works.
   Separately, `.hooks(...)` there produced
   "error[E0277]: the `?` operator cannot be applied to type `App`", so unlike
   the neighbouring builder calls it is not fallible.

4. A plain `pre_dispatch` hook receives the root `ArgMatches`, not the
   subcommand's. Reading the flag directly panicked with:
   "Mismatch between definition and access of `answers`. Unknown argument or
   group id." framework-integration.md promises this walk only for `.input(...)`
   ("Walks to the deepest subcommand's `ArgMatches` (so chains see the same args
   the handler does)"); for a hand-written hook I had to call
   `get_deepest_matches` myself.

5. The built-in confirmation gate contradicts this app's spec. Under a pty,
   answering `y` produced:
   "Continue? Type 'yes' to continue: y
    Hook error: hook error (pre-dispatch): questionnaire confirmation declined;
    nothing was run"
   while SPEC.md requires "`yes` or `y` (case-insensitive) confirms". See the
   workarounds answer for how that is resolved.

6. Error text is doubled up: every guard failure is reported as
   "Hook error: hook error (pre-dispatch): ...". The message content is right
   and the exit status is 1, but the prefix is noisier than an application would
   choose, and there is no documented way to shape it.

answers.summary:
`formlike` is complete and behaves to spec; `cargo build` and `cargo test` both
pass and I verified every path by running the binary (including interactive and
confirmation paths under a real pty).

The three questions are a standout questionnaire derived from a Rust struct
(`ProvisionAnswers`, questionnaire id `formlike.provision`), with a
`QuestionnaireChoices` enum for `region` and a field validator for `name`. That
gives the framework-generated surface for free: `provision questions` renders
the blank sheet with the stable id tags, `--answers FILE` / `--answers -` read
one completed sheet, blank answers take defaults, and every source decodes
through the same pipeline. The handler is a thin adapter that renders one line,
`provisioned NAME in REGION (public: yes|no)`.

Two guards on top of the framework make unattended runs fail promptly rather
than block or under-explain:

- a pre-dispatch hook that runs before questionnaire resolution and rejects a
  run with no sheet and no attended terminal, naming the three question ids and
  the `--answers` flag that would have unblocked it;
- this program's own confirmation gate, because the spec accepts `y` as well as
  `yes` (case-insensitive) and the framework's built-in gate accepts only an
  exact `yes`.

Exit codes are as specified: 0 on success, 1 for every input error (missing
required answer, validation failure, impossible collection, impossible or
declined confirmation), 2 for clap usage errors. A non-interactive successful
run writes exactly one line to stdout and nothing to stderr.
answers.workarounds:
1. Synthesized `--yes`. Because the framework's confirmation gate accepts only
   an exact `yes` and the spec also accepts `y`, `dispatch_args` appends `--yes`
   to the arguments handed to `App::run` for a bare `provision` run, which turns
   the framework gate off, and `confirm_gate` then asks the question itself with
   the spec's rule. The hook distinguishes a user-supplied `--yes` from the
   synthesized one by reading the real `std::env::args()`. `dispatch_args`
   deliberately does not touch `provision questions`, `help provision`, or any
   `--help` run, and it skips flag values so a sheet named `questions` is not
   mistaken for the subcommand; the three cases are unit-tested.

2. Framework-internal argument id. `has_answer_sheet` decides whether a sheet
   was supplied by looking for a parsed argument id ending in
   `questionnaire_answers`, with a scan of argv for `--answers` as a fallback.
   A public accessor for the injected flag would replace both halves.

3. Prompt stream split. The framework writes its interactive question prompts to
   stdout, so an attended collection run has prompt text on stdout ahead of the
   success line; SPEC.md calls interactive prompt layout cosmetic, and I found
   no way to redirect it. This app's own confirmation prompt goes to stderr
   instead, which keeps stdout to exactly the one success line for every
   non-interactive run.
